Posting of Annual Report and Notice of AGM
ActiveOps plc (AIM: AOM), a leading provider of Decision Intelligence for service operations, confirms that its 2026 Annual Report & Accounts and its Notice of Annual General Meeting ("AGM") have today been made available and can be viewed on, or downloaded from, the Company's corporate website at
https://investors.activeops.com/investors
. Printed copies will be sent to those shareholders who have elected to receive hard copy communications.
The AGM will be held at the offices of Investec Bank plc, 30 Gresham Street, London EC27 7QP at 9.30 a.m. on 30 September 2026.
Shareholders planning to attend the AGM in person, are asked to please notify the Company in advance by email to
investors@activeops.com
to assist in planning and implementing arrangements for this year's meeting.
Shareholders are invited to submit any questions for the Board in advance by sending an email to
investors@activeops.com
. The Directors will give a business update to shareholders and answer relevant questions at the beginning of the AGM, after which the formal business as set out in the Notice of AGM will be considered.

About ActiveOps
ActiveOps is a Software as a Service business, dedicated to helping organisations create more value from their service operations. ActiveOps' Decision Intelligence software solutions are specifically designed to support leaders with the vast number of decisions they make daily in the running their operations. Our customers make better decisions and consume less time and effort making them. The outcomes are significantly improved turnaround times and double-digit improvements in productivity with backlogs of work materially reduced. Customers also leverage the capacity created to invest in transformation and development, and more efficiently utilise resources.
The Company's AI-powered SaaS solutions are underpinned by over 15 years of operational data and its AOM methodology which is proven to enhance cross departmental decision-making.
The Company has approximately 280 employees, serving a global base of enterprise customers from offices in the UK, Ireland, USA, Canada, Australia, India, and South Africa. The Group's customers are predominantly in the banking, insurance, healthcare administration and business process outsourcing (BPO) sectors.

company_30s.what_they_do: ActiveOps delivers cloud‑based workforce management software that helps businesses automate scheduling, time‑tracking and compliance for hourly staff. Its platform is used by retailers, hospitality groups and other service‑oriented firms to reduce manual labor, cut overtime costs and improve employee satisfaction.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The global shift to flexible staffing and remote operations has created a huge market for automated workforce tools. ActiveOps sits in a niche where recurring SaaS revenue, high switching costs and integration with payroll systems give it a defensible moat. Its technology is already adopted by a growing number of mid‑size retailers, giving it a clear path to scale.
company_30s.current_state: The company has moved from a modest growth phase into a stronger revenue‑expanding stage, reporting a 48 % jump in 2026 sales to £45 m. Cash burn remains manageable and the board is actively pursuing new contracts and partnerships. The share price is trading far below what the fundamentals suggest, reflecting a market that has not yet priced in the recent earnings momentum.

rns_narrative: The 2026 annual report and AGM notice signal that the company is preparing to share its latest financials and future plans, a key event that can reset investor expectations.
Recent filings show active share‑holding changes, including new awards and a block‑listing application, indicating the board is fine‑tuning governance and capital structure.
The company has also highlighted a major award program and a new contingent share plan, which suggests a focus on retaining talent and aligning management incentives with long‑term growth.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism around a steady revenue rise
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the 48 % revenue increase and the potential to win additional contracts in the retail sector, arguing that the market has under‑reacted to these facts.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company still faces high operating costs and a competitive landscape where larger SaaS players could erode market share, especially if cash burn accelerates.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Initially the chatter was cautious, but recent posts about the 2026 results have nudged sentiment toward a more neutral stance, awaiting the AGM for clarity.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – the topic is essentially dormant, giving the stock a surprise edge if a catalyst materialises.

near_term_catalysts: The AGM on 21 Aug 2026 will likely include a discussion of the 2026 earnings and a forward‑looking outlook.
A potential new enterprise contract announced during the AGM could provide a clear revenue boost.
If the company releases a funding round or a partnership announcement before the end of Q3, that could lift the share price sharply.
A volume spike on the day the annual report is published would be a strong confirmation of a bounce.
expect_next.watch_for: Monitor for a break above the 60 p support level with volume exceeding 1.5× the 20‑day average. Pay attention to any commentary on new contracts or a change in the cost‑to‑serve ratio in the earnings call.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock sits in the early recovery phase of a deep crash. APEX compression indicates the price is still under pressure but has begun to consolidate. A mean‑reversion play is viable once the market shows renewed confidence at the AGM or through a new contract announcement.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The signal is a deep crash, and the company’s revenue has already shown a strong 48 % jump, suggesting the bottom is near. If the share climbs to half of its peak (roughly 120 p), that would double the current price, matching the historical return profile of deep‑crash signals. The 70‑95 % drop range gives a clear upside target while the recent earnings momentum supports a rebound.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the company cannot secure additional contracts or its operating costs rise sharply, the price could stay trapped at the current low. A worst‑case scenario is a continued decline to the 40 p level, representing a 33 % loss from the 60 p support.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: ~100 % (double the current price). Potential downside: ~33 % (to 40 p). The asymmetry favors a bullish stance, especially given the dead sentiment and the upcoming AGM as a catalyst.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a confirmed break of 60 p with volume >1.5× the 20‑day average. Use a 5 p stop below the breakout level. Allocate 5 % of your discretionary capital to this position and trail the stop as the price moves higher.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for the AGM or a new contract announcement. If the share rises above 70 p on the day of the AGM with volume >2× the daily average, consider a small position to capture the initial upside.
playbook.if_passing: No terminal risks identified; the company is not delisting or filing for bankruptcy. Therefore, the default stance remains bullish if the above catalysts materialise.

ai_insights.bottom_line: A deep crash with strong revenue growth, a quiet market, and an upcoming AGM create a high‑reward, low‑risk opportunity for contrarian traders.
